title: Thermodynamic Framework for $q$-Affinity
abstract: We develop a thermodynamic framework for non-equilibrium affinities based on generalized entropies. In particular, we extend the classical concept of De Donder by introducing $q$-affinities associated with Rényi and Tsallis entropies. This in turn allows us to generalize thermodynamic driving forces to systems with long-range interactions and/or strong correlations. For Rényi entropy, we build on a thermodynamic interpretation due to Baez, where the entropy is expressed through finite differences of the Helmholtz free energy at two temperatures. This leads to a generalized thermodynamic potential whose derivative with respect to a reaction coordinate defines the Rényi $q$-affinity. The resulting expression admits a representation in terms of exponential work averages, establishing a connection to Jarzynski-type fluctuation relations. For Tsallis entropy, we consider Markov jump processes using a master-equation-based approach. We derive a $q$-deformed entropy balance law and obtain an explicit expression for the Tsallis entropy production rate, proving its non-negativity and thus recovering a generalized second-law structure. This allows to identify a local stochastic $q$-affinity with the generalized thermodynamic force entering the entropy production rate.
summary: This paper constructs a generalized thermodynamic framework using Rényi and Tsallis entropies to define $q$-affinities for non-equilibrium processes. It successfully extends the second law of thermodynamics to systems exhibiting strong correlations or non-Gibbsian statistics by deriving non-negative entropy production rates. This provides essential theoretical tools for analyzing complex, far-from-equilibrium physical systems.
main_problem: The paper develops a generalized thermodynamic framework for non-equilibrium affinities, extending classical concepts to systems with long-range interactions or strong correlations.
main_result: It successfully derives $q$-affinities based on Rényi and Tsallis entropies, establishing a generalized second law structure ($\dot{S}_i \ge 0$) for these non-extensive systems.
method: The authors use master equation approaches and thermodynamic identities involving generalized entropies (Rényi/Tsallis) to define $q$-deformed entropy balance laws and affinities.
model_or_system: The framework applies to general non-equilibrium systems, particularly those undergoing Markov jump processes or described by reaction equilibria, moving beyond the standard Gibbsian assumptions.
key_observables: Generalized thermodynamic force ($q$-affinity, $A^q$), Entropy Production Rate ($\dot{S}_i(T)_q$), and generalized free energy potentials ($\Phi_q$).
important_parameters: The non-extensivity parameter $q$, which governs the deviation from standard Boltzmann/Shannon statistics.
main_assumptions: The framework relies on extending classical irreversible thermodynamics using non-extensive generalizations, assuming a Markovian embedding for local stochastic definitions.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the generalized affinity for Rényi entropy via free energy differences, then tackling Tsallis entropy using master equations to derive the entropy production rate. Finally, it consolidates these findings into a general $q$-deformed entropy balance law.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful mathematical tools (generalized affinities and entropies) applicable to open quantum systems where non-Markovian or long-range effects invalidate standard thermodynamic descriptions.
